dbcHistory.message: webhud: implement map tile fetching and caching for improved road segment access

webhud: live car controls that send over IBUS1, and the HUD from the car's own buses

The car-control menus are live on the car: each control follows what the car reports (doors, liftgate,
windows, sunroof, mirrors, lights, climate, seat heat, gear, drive mode, battery, charging), the 3D car
follows the same values, and setting a control sends the head unit's own control message through the
Android app's CAN link (windows auto up/down, lock, liftgate, sunroof position, mirrors, lamps,
climate, seat heat and moves, the locking settings). Controls the car has no message for, or whose
message the head unit sends itself every second, or whose frame would carry every audio volume along,
are greyed with the reason. Energy shows the charging power, pack voltage and current, time left,
limits and health. Doors are manual now: only the liftgate has buttons; the windows have held up/down
buttons.

The tables, the IBUS DBC and the app's ID lists are generated from the FM29 IBUS matrices by
tools/gen_ibus.py, with the matrix's LSB start bits converted to DBC numbering (the hand-made table
was only right for signals inside one byte). The gateway mirrors the ADAS bus onto IBUS2 with the same
layout, so the page's worker keeps a second decoder on the IBUS DBC and the HUD runs from the car alone
whenever the comma's ticks aren't coming (CAR in the mode chip).

The CAN helper transmits only the IDs it is given (checked again in the app), with loopback off, and
repeats every message's current frame once a second so steady values (climate, seats, a window's
position) no longer expire in the page. Its output now goes through one locked writer: a race on the
buffered writer had been dropping everything after the first frame.
